question.text: Under the SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, the use of derivatives by a portfolio manager is:

answer.text: Primarily for hedging and portfolio rebalancing, through recognised stock exchanges and subject to the Portfolio Management Agreement and disclosure-document requirements

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook permits portfolio managers to invest in derivatives, including for the purposes of hedging and portfolio rebalancing, through recognised stock exchanges. The terms of such investments must be set out in the Portfolio Management Agreement, including exposure limits, and must be disclosed in the disclosure document. Prior permission of the client is required for any change to those terms. The Trap: "Unlimited" ignores the agreement-level exposure limits and disclosure obligations. "Prohibited" is wrong - derivatives are explicitly allowed for hedging and rebalancing. "Arbitrage only" is not the framing used by the workbook. Note: Source - NISM-Series-XXI-B Portfolio Managers Certification Examination workbook (Sep 2025), p. 108.
